land.text: the island, which Cliopatria's Chola shape holds to 1093 and the Chola dossier closes in 1070

predecessors.note: Polonnaruwa page: Vijayabahu I took Anuradhapura and then Polonnaruwa 'after a siege of isolated Chola forces' by 1070. The Anuradhapura Kingdom (to 1017) is the earlier Sinhalese state; the Chola held the island between.

land.text: the northern realm (Rajarata, the Vanni and the Jaffna peninsula) that Magha kept after 1236

successors.note: Infobox successor 'Jaffna Kingdom' and 'Vanni chieftaincies'; Cliopatria's Jaffna kingdom row starts in 1314, so 1237-1313 has no row for this land.

land.text: the Polonnaruwa core, from which Magha was expelled in 1236 'in a southern invasion'

successors.note: Infobox successor 'Kingdom of Dambadeniya'; the page says Vijayabahu III established it in 1232 over Maya Rata, which does not overlap Polonnaruwa's outline. It does not name who held Polonnaruwa after 1236.

capitals.name: Polonnaruwa (Vijayarajapura)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Vijayarajapura'; text Polonnaruwa; Vijayabahu I 'kept Polonnaruwa as his capital'. Between 1111 and 1152 the court of Rajarata sits here (Vikramabahu I, Gajabahu II) on the Parakramabahu page's Rajarata.

capitals.name: Jaffna peninsula (Magha)
capitals.note: Magha 'moved the capital to the Jaffna peninsula'; the page also has him expelled from Polonnaruwa in 1236.

rulers.name: Gajabahu II
rulers.note: 'succeeded to the throne of Rajarata' in 1132; abdicated before Parakramabahu's coronation

correction.text: the whole island, as Cliopatria draws it from 1072, carried back to 1070

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1070-1071: Cliopatria's row starts in 1072, but the page says 'By 1070, when Sinhalese sovereignty was restored under Vijayabahu I' the island was reunited: Anuradhapura 'quickly fell' and Polonnaruwa was taken after a siege of the isolated Chola forces. The 1072 outline (the whole island) is carried back two years; confidence 2 because the page says 'by 1070'. The infobox 'Established' is 1055 (Vijayabahu 'crowned himself in 1055 at Anuradhapura'), but the page gives no land for 1055-1069, so the state is drawn from 1070 (see notes).

correction.text: the whole island, unchanged, for 1072-1110 only; the row's later years are replaced by the keyframes for 1111, 1153 and 1197

keyframe_review.note: Applies 1072-1110. 243 cells: the whole island (239 of the 239 cells of the gazetteer's Sri Lanka (island)) and 4 rim cells off the coast; Cliopatria holds this one outline to 1249. The page supports it only while Vijayabahu I reigns (1055-1111 in the infobox, 1055-1110 in the text; 'island was reunited' by 1070). For 1111-1152 the Parakramabahu I page says 'the island was divided into three kingdoms' and Polonnaruwa kept only Rajarata, so the outline is replaced there (new keyframe 1111); it returns for 1153-1196 (new keyframe 1153).

correction.text: Rajarata, the northern third of the island round Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa; the page names the kingdom but gives no boundary, so Cliopatria's 1250 northern outline stands in

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1111-1152: Cliopatria still draws the whole island. The Parakramabahu I page says that 'By the reign of Vikramabahu I (1111-1132)', 'the island was divided into three kingdoms': Rajarata (Vikramabahu, then his son Gajabahu II from 1132), Dakkhinadesa (Malaya Rata, Manabharana, then Kitti Sri Megha) and Ruhuna (Sri Vallabha and Kitti Sri Megha, then Sri Vallabha alone). Polonnaruwa's kingdom is Rajarata. The page gives no boundary for Rajarata; the stand-in is Cliopatria's 1250-1259 northern outline (93 cells: Anuradhapura 27, Polonnaruwa 6 of 13, Mullaittivu 9, Vavuniya 8, Trincomalee 9, Matale 7, Mannar 7, Puttalam 5, Kilinochchi 4, Jaffna 3, Kurunegala 3, Kandy 2 and 3 rim cells), which covers the Anuradhapura-Polonnaruwa core and the Vanni; the page names Rajarata but does not bound it. Confidence 1 for the edges.

New keyframe 1153-1196: the whole island again. 'Following a protracted civil war, he secured power over the entire island around 1153' and Parakramabahu I became 'the unquestioned lord of the entire island'; the Polonnaruwa page ends the last single-island rule with Nissanka Malla's death in 1196. The outline is Cliopatria's 1072 shape unchanged (the same years it already covers); only the years differ. Two revolts and a raid did not move the line: Ruhuna 1156-1158 and the 'brief insurrection in 1160' (Parakramabahu I page; the Polonnaruwa page calls the 1160 rising 'formidable'), and Mantota 1168-1169.

correction.text: the northern outline (Rajarata, the Vanni and the Jaffna peninsula) for 1197-1236; the south is no longer Polonnaruwa's

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1197-1236: after the last single-island rule ends in 1196 the page gives no map. The Parakramabahu I page says only that the successors were weak and 'the chronic instability and the renewal of the civil war' undid his work. The Polonnaruwa page has Parakrama Pandyan II (Pandyan-backed rival claimant, 1212-1215) seize the capital in 1212, and Kalinga Magha invade in 1215 and move the capital to the Jaffna peninsula. The northern outline (Rajarata and the Vanni, with Jaffna) is the only part the page ties to the kingdom, so Cliopatria's 1250 shape is drawn from 1197 to the end in 1236. Confidence 1: the page names no frontier. Maya Rata, where Vijayabahu III 'established the Kingdom of Dambadeniya in 1232', does not overlap this outline (Cliopatria's Dambadeniya shape of 1236: 0 shared cells).

correction.text: the same northern outline, but for 1237-1259 it is the rump of Magha's realm and the origin of the Jaffna and Vanni states, not the Kingdom of Polonnaruwa

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1250-1259 shape (26,794 km2, 93 cells, the north) falls after this dossier's end in 1236: the text says Magha 'was expelled from Polonnaruwa in 1236' (infobox 'Disestablished' 1232), and 'After his death in 1255, Polonnaruwa ceased to be the capital'. The same outline is used for 1197-1236; for 1237-1259 it belongs to Magha's northern rump (the page's successors 'Jaffna Kingdom' and 'Vanni chieftaincies'), which no Cliopatria row covers before Jaffna kingdom (1314).

region.text: the whole island, as the 1072 outline

ledger.note: By 1070: Sinhalese sovereignty is restored under Vijayabahu I. 'By 1070, when Sinhalese sovereignty was restored under Vijayabahu I', the island was reunited; Anuradhapura 'quickly fell' and Polonnaruwa was taken after a siege of the isolated Chola forces; the text has the kingdom expanding 'from 1070 until 1232'. The infobox gives 'Established' 1055 and Vijayabahu 'crowned himself in 1055 at Anuradhapura' (the page contradicts itself on the crowning place and keeps Polonnaruwa as his capital), but names no land for 1055-1069, so the dossier starts in 1070. Chola Empire is the counterpart (the page names Virarajendra Chola).

region.text: Dakkhinadesa (Malaya Rata) and Ruhuna, the island south of Rajarata; Cliopatria's 1250 northern outline stands in for Rajarata

ledger.note: 1111: the island splits in three. 'By the reign of Vikramabahu I (1111-1132)', 'the island was divided into three kingdoms', Rajarata, Dakkhinadesa (Malaya Rata) and Ruhuna; the Polonnaruwa page lists Vijayabahu I to 1111 (text 1110). The page gives no boundary, so the lost land is the island outside the Rajarata stand-in (150 cells). The date is the start of Vikramabahu's reign, not a dated event.

region.text: Dakkhinadesa (Malaya Rata) and Ruhuna, the island south of Rajarata

ledger.note: c. 1153: Parakramabahu I reunites the island. 'Around 1150 AD, Parakramabahu made his first move' (taking Malaya); 'Following a protracted civil war, he secured power over the entire island around 1153'; he was crowned (infobox 1153) and became 'the unquestioned lord of the entire island'. The page gives the war's length as 'over a decade' in one passage and 'around five years of incessant warfare' in another. Land: the Dakkhinadesa and Ruhuna that split off in 1111, bounded only by the Rajarata stand-in.

region.text: Rameswaram and the shore near Ramanathapuram

ledger.counterpart: Pandya kingdom of Madurai (Kulasekhara's side in the Pandyan civil war)
ledger.note: c. 1167: Sinhalese troops take Rameswaram in the Pandyan war. The Pandyan king 'appealed to his namesake in Sri Lanka for assistance' (the page gives 1167 as the start); the general Lankapura Dandanatha 'landed in the vicinity of Ramanathapuram' and 'captured the city of Rameswaram'. The Polonnaruwa page: Rameswaram 'was under Sinhalese and Vira Pandyan Alliance rule till 1182'. Neither page dates the capture; 1167 is the war's start. The Cholas are the counterpart because the war 'ended in favour of the Cholas'; the pages also name Kulasekhara, who 'had captured the capital city of Madurai', and the Vira Pandyan side. Cliopatria's Chola shape of 1170 does not contain this land. The radius is a rough figure for the island and the nearby mainland shore. [Reviewer sa-03-g, 2026-10-19: counterpart changed from chola-empire: Rameswaram lay in the Pandya country fought over in the Pandyan succession war (Parakramabahu I page: 'the Pandyan king Parakrama appealed to his namesake in Sri Lanka'), and Cliopatria's Chola shape has none of these cells in 1167-1182; the Cholas backed the other side.]

region.text: Rameswaram and the shore near Ramanathapuram

ledger.counterpart: Pandya kingdom of Madurai (Kulasekhara's side in the Pandyan civil war)
ledger.note: 1182: Rameswaram leaves Sinhalese hands. 'Rameshwaram was under Sinhalese and Vira Pandyan Alliance rule till 1182', the year of the Tirukkollambudur record (4th year of Kulottunga III): 'The town of Madura was captured and made over to Vikrama Pandya.' The war itself 'ended in favour of the Cholas, sometime in the 1170s'. The page does not say who took Rameswaram. [Reviewer sa-03-g, 2026-10-19: counterpart changed from chola-empire: Rameswaram lay in the Pandya country fought over in the Pandyan succession war (Parakramabahu I page: 'the Pandyan king Parakrama appealed to his namesake in Sri Lanka'), and Cliopatria's Chola shape has none of these cells in 1167-1182; the Cholas backed the other side.]

region.text: the island south of Rajarata, no longer ruled from Polonnaruwa after 1196

ledger.note: 1196: the last single-island rule ends. The page puts the end of Polonnaruwa's last single-island rule at Nissanka Malla's death in 1196 (reign 1187-1196, another passage 1197). It names no holder of the south and no frontier, so the land is the island outside the Rajarata stand-in and the counterpart is nobody.

1212: a Pandyan-backed claimant seizes the capital. 'In 1212, the capital was seized by' Parakrama Pandyan II, with Pandyan assistance; the page lists him as a rival claimant for 1212-1215. The month is not on the page.

1215: Kalinga Magha invades. The page ends Parakrama Pandyan II's span in 1215, the year Magha 'invaded the kingdom with the help of his soldiers and mercenaries' from Kalinga, Kerala and Damila (Tamil Nadu). The page does not say how the claimant fell.

1215: Magha moves the capital north. He 'moved the capital to the Jaffna peninsula'. The page words it as a move 'as a tribute-paying subordinate of the Chola Empire at Tanjavur' (no end, no terms; Cliopatria's Chola shape does not reach the island, so no vassal tint is drawn). The same page says Magha was 'expelled from Polonnaruwa in 1236', so he still held the old capital as well; the page does not square the two.

region.text: the northern realm of 1197-1236: Rajarata, the Vanni and the Jaffna peninsula

ledger.note: 1236: Magha is expelled from Polonnaruwa. The text: 'expelled from Polonnaruwa in 1236' in a southern invasion (the infobox says 'Disestablished' 1232, the Magha span there is 1215-1232, and Vijayabahu III 'established the Kingdom of Dambadeniya in 1232'). The infobox successors are the Kingdom of Dambadeniya, the Jaffna Kingdom and the Vanni chieftaincies; the northern land passes to Magha's rump, the later Jaffna kingdom. 1255 (Magha's death) is when 'Polonnaruwa ceased to be the capital'.

wars.name: Parakramabahu I's war of unification

zones.text: Dakkhinadesa (Malaya Rata) and Ruhuna, the island south of Rajarata

wars.outcome: Parakramabahu I takes Malaya around 1150 and 'secured power over the entire island around 1153'; the three kingdoms of 1111 become one.
wars.note: The page gives the length as 'over a decade' and as 'around five years of incessant warfare'; 1150 and 1153 are its two dated points.

wars.name: Ruhuna revolt and the 1160 insurrection
wars.outcome: Put down; Ruhuna stayed quiet afterwards except for 'a brief insurrection in 1160' (Parakramabahu I page); the Polonnaruwa page calls the 1160 rising 'formidable'. No border moved.
wars.note: Revolt of 1156-1158 on the Parakramabahu I page; the two pages disagree on the size of the 1160 rising.

wars.name: Burma campaign of Parakramabahu I
wars.outcome: 'The first navy was organized in 1165. This was used for the invasion of Burma.' The raid took 'several other cities, including Arimaddhanapura'; no land was held.
wars.note: The Parakramabahu I page links the raid to the reign of Narathu (1167-1171) and gives Coedes's date of 1180; 1165 and 1180 are the two page dates. Belligerent named 'Ramanna (Burma)' on the Polonnaruwa page.

wars.name: Pandyan Civil War (Sinhalese intervention)

zones.text: Rameswaram and the shore near Ramanathapuram

wars.outcome: The war 'ended in favour of the Cholas, sometime in the 1170s'; Rameswaram stayed under Sinhalese and Vira Pandyan rule until 1182.
wars.note: The Polonnaruwa page headlines the Pandyan Civil War as 1169-1177; the Parakramabahu I page gives 1167 for the appeal. The pages name Kulasekhara, the Cholas (who won), Vira Pandya and the general Lankapura Dandanatha; the extracts do not spell out the sides.

wars.name: Rebellion at Mantota
wars.outcome: The only rebellion of the reign outside Ruhuna, 'in the region of modern Mantota in from 1168-1169'; no border moved.
wars.note: The Polonnaruwa page has a 'rebellion in 1168' in Rajarata.

wars.name: Pandyan claimant at Polonnaruwa
wars.outcome: Parakrama Pandyan II seizes the capital in 1212 with Pandyan help and reigns to 1215, when Magha invades.

wars.name: Kalinga Magha's invasion
wars.outcome: Magha 'invaded the kingdom with the help of his soldiers and mercenaries' in 1215 and ruled from the north until he was 'expelled from Polonnaruwa in 1236'.
wars.note: The infobox gives Magha 1215-1232 and the end of the kingdom in 1232; the text 1215-1236.

certainty.note: Neither page draws a frontier; the island coast is the only hard edge, and Rajarata's southern limit is a stand-in.

notes: WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's Polonnaruwa row (1072-1259) draws two shapes: the whole island for 1072-1249 (243 cells, 239 on the island) and a northern outline for 1250-1259 (93 cells; 26,794 km2). The pages support the island only for 1070-1110 and 1153-1196. FROM 1111 TO 1152 the Parakramabahu I page divides the island into three kingdoms and Polonnaruwa keeps Rajarata. FROM 1197 the page names no frontier; the northern outline is used to 1236. START AND END. The infobox gives 1055 to 1232; the text 'from 1070 until 1232', Magha 'expelled from Polonnaruwa in 1236' and 'After his death in 1255, Polonnaruwa ceased to be the capital'. This dossier starts in 1070 (the first year the pages give land; the Chola dossier closes the island to Cholas in 1070) and ends in 1236 (loss of the capital town), where Cliopatria runs to 1259. Pages opened: 2 of 2 (Polonnaruwa, Parakramabahu I). NOT SETTLED. (1) Vijayabahu I's own page was not opened (budget), so the Rohana enclave of 1055-1069 is not drawn. (2) The Rajarata boundary is not on either page. (3) The Cliopatria Ceylon and Dambadeniya rows (1236-1259) overlap the island's south and are not touched here. (4) Magha as a 'tribute-paying subordinate' of the Cholas is the page's wording only; it is kept in the 1215 capital_move note and no vassal tint is drawn. HAND-OFFS. The Chola dossier has no entry for the Rameswaram episode of 1167-1182 (this dossier uses chola-empire as the counterpart); the Jaffna-kingdom dossier should cover the north for 1237-1313.
